frozen_original.description_long: The Associated Press reported that President Donald Trump sought naval assistance from allies to reopen the Strait of Hormuz during the 2026 Iran war. The report described his demand as an effort to enlist partners after the United States and Israel began military operations without consulting them. Britain initially refused the use of its bases for attacks, later allowing U.S. strikes on Iran’s ballistic-missile program, while Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Britain would not be drawn into the wider conflict without international-law support and a considered plan. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said sending more warships would not help a diplomatic solution. French President Emmanuel Macron said France was not joining the war and would consider escorts only after fighting subsided. AP reported no close ally had offered immediate assistance and quoted officials and analysts describing frustration with the demand and its delivery. This captures the reported disagreement and allied responses; “bluster” is an editorial characterization, and the article does not establish a measurable long-term loss of U.S. standing.

proposal.description_long: In August 2023, prosecutors in the federal election case against Donald Trump asked a judge in Washington to impose a protective order governing the use and disclosure of discovery materials. The Justice Department argued that public disclosure of evidence such as grand-jury interviews or sealed-warrant materials could chill witnesses or affect the administration of justice. The filing cited Trump’s history of social media posts about judges, lawyers and witnesses in his cases, including a Truth Social message stating, “If you go after me, I’m coming after you.” Trump’s defense described the post as political speech and contested the request. This procedural request concerned access to evidence exchanged in discovery; it was not itself a gag order covering all public statements and did not establish that the posts were criminal conduct. Other reporting in September 2023 described a separate request to restrict statements about participants in the election case. The supplied Washington Post link is an October 2023 catalogue, but its article body was not readable in the focused review. The revised title and account describe the documented protective-order request and avoid an unsupported count of “dozens” or a legal conclusion about obstruction. A final order should be consulted before describing the precise restrictions imposed.
proposal.description_medium: In August 2023, special counsel Jack Smith asked the court in Washington to restrict how Donald Trump and his lawyers could disclose materials received in discovery in the 2020 election case. Prosecutors cited Trump’s history of posting about people involved in his cases and pointed to a Truth Social post reading, “If you go after me, I’m coming after you.” Trump’s lawyers argued the post was political speech. The filing documents the prosecutors’ request and stated concern, not a judicial finding that the posts constituted obstruction or witness intimidation.
proposal.description_short: Prosecutors cited Trump’s social media posts in seeking a discovery protective order in the 2020 election case; the filing was not a finding that the posts were crimes.

proposal.description_long: The Associated Press reports that Yosemite National Park ranger and biologist Shannon “SJ” Joslin was fired after hanging a large transgender pride flag on El Capitan in May 2025. AP says Joslin and other climbers displayed the flag for about two hours and removed it voluntarily. A termination letter cited failure to demonstrate acceptable conduct in Joslin’s role as a biologist and referred to the May incident; Joslin said the action was taken as a private citizen. The article also reports that other Yosemite employees were placed on administrative leave while the park investigated. These details support a focused account of Joslin’s firing and the stated basis in the termination letter, with the employee’s characterization separately attributed. The article does not establish that federal agencies broadly fired transgender employees or workers who supported trans rights, nor does it document the additional examples in the broader original title. Narrowing the title to the AP-documented Yosemite case keeps the entry within the evidence. Any broader pattern would require separate agency records and case-specific reporting.
proposal.description_medium: The AP reports that Yosemite ranger and biologist Shannon “SJ” Joslin was fired after helping hang a large transgender pride flag on El Capitan in May 2025. The termination letter cited unacceptable conduct and the flag incident; Joslin said the display was in a personal capacity. The article documents one case, not a pattern across federal agencies.
proposal.description_short: AP reports Yosemite ranger Shannon “SJ” Joslin was fired after hanging a transgender pride flag; this single case does not establish a broader pattern.

limitations: One case does not demonstrate a government-wide campaign or establish broader agency motives.

The staged and effective rows remain needs_context at revision 2. The official U.S. Sentencing Commission chair’s January 24 remarks say Judges Claria Horn Boom and John Gleeson’s service ended earlier that month, but do not say President Trump removed them; this documents two departures, not the alleged three firings on January 20 (https://www.ussc.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/amendment-process/public-hearings-and-meetings/20250124/remarks.pdf).

The Commission’s January 24 release gives its membership at that meeting but supplies no notice that Trump removed three commissioners (https://www.ussc.gov/about/news/press-releases/january-24-2025). The official record does not establish who the alleged three people were, whether they were fired, or the date and reason.

28 U.S.C. § 991(a) does state that Commission members may be removed only for neglect of duty, malfeasance, or other good cause, but the statute does not prove a removal or litigation over one (https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A28+section%3A991+edition%3Aprelim%29+OR+%28granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title28-section991%29&f=treesort&num=0&edition=prelim).

Hold until a primary termination/removal communication or reliable contemporaneous report identifies the affected commissioners and establishes an actual Trump removal; any claimed legal dispute also needs its case filing or docket and procedural status. Do not transfer facts from removals involving another commission.
